chapter.title: Windows
chapter.para: On Windows, the bridge reaches the desktop framework (Windows Forms, WPF, system dialogs) and COM objects (Office, WMI, the scripting objects). These programs need Windows, and the .NET Desktop Runtime for the windows.

section.title: A Window
section.para: You want a window with a few controls, whose events run Rexx methods.

example.title: A Window
example.programlisting:
forms = .net~System~Windows~Forms drawing = .net~System~Drawing form = forms~Form~new form~Text = "Hello from Rexx" form~ClientSize = drawing~Size~new(300, 90) form~StartPosition = "CenterScreen" box = forms~TextBox~new box~Location = drawing~Point~new(12, 12); box~Width = 180 button = forms~Button~new button~Text = "Greet"; button~Location = drawing~Point~new(204, 10) label = forms~Label~new label~Location = drawing~Point~new(12, 50); label~AutoSize = .true form~Controls~Add(box); form~Controls~Add(button); form~Controls~Add(label) form~AcceptButton = button button~Click += .net~handler(.Greeter~new(box, label), "CLICK") forms~Application~Run(form)
::requires "net.cls" ::class Greeter ::method init expose box label use arg box, label ::method click expose box label use arg sender, e label~Text = "Hello," box~Text"!"

section.para: How it works. Controls are .NET objects, set up through their properties (an enum property takes the value's name: "CenterScreen"), and a Click handler is a Rexx method. Application~Run(form) shows the window and runs its events on this thread until it closes; the handler runs on it too, nested in that call. The sample windows/forms-hello.rex is this program, a little longer.
See also Reference, Callbacks, Events and Tasks, Windows, Linux and macOS.

section.title: Message Boxes and File Dialogs
section.para: You want to ask the user something, or to let them choose a file.

example.title: Message Boxes and File Dialogs
example.programlisting:
forms = .net~System~Windows~Forms answer = forms~MessageBox~Show("Do you like Rexx?", "Question", "YesNo", "Question") if answer = "Yes" then say "Of course." d = forms~OpenFileDialog~new d~Filter = "Rexx programs (*.rex)|*.rex|All files (*.*)|*.*" if d~ShowDialog = "OK" then say "You chose" d~FileName
::requires "net.cls"

section.para: How it works. MessageBox.Show takes its buttons and its icon as enum names, and answers the button chosen, a DialogResult compared with its name. The common dialogs need a single-threaded apartment, which the bridge makes every Rexx thread on Windows.
See also Reference, Windows, Linux and macOS.

section.title: Excel, as with OLEObject
section.para: You want to drive Excel (or Word, or any automation server), and handle its events.

example.title: Excel, as with OLEObject
example.programlisting:
excel = .net~createObject("Excel.Application") book = excel~Workbooks~Add sheet = book~Worksheets~Item(1) grid = .array~new(2, 2) grid[1, 1] = "Item"; grid[1, 2] = "Price" grid[2, 1] = "Tea"; grid[2, 2] = 3.5 sheet~Range("A1:B2")~Value = grid sheet~Range("B3")~Formula = "=SUM(B2:B2)" say sheet~Range("B3")~Value back = sheet~Range("A1:B2")~Value -- a .NET object[,] from 1 (COM's) say back[2, 1] back[2, 2] back~dimensions~makeString("L", "x") back~GetLowerBound(0) book~Close(.false); excel~Quit; .net~releaseObject(excel)
::requires "net.cls"

section.para: How it works. .net~createObject(progID) is .OLEObject~new(progID), with the same messages. A two-dimensional Rexx Array goes to Excel as a two-dimensional SAFEARRAY, a whole range at once; reading the range's Value gives one back, a NetArray from 1 in both dimensions (its .NET lower bounds are 1 too, as COM's). Calls are made in English, as VBA's are, so =SUM(...) works on any Windows. .net~releaseObject(excel) lets Excel's process end now. The project's samples/office has Excel, Word and PowerPoint programs written twice, with OLEObject and through the bridge, events included.

section.title: Asking Windows About Itself
section.para: You want information about the computer: its system, its disks, its processes.

example.title: Asking Windows About Itself
example.programlisting:
wmi = .net~getObject("winmgmts:\\.\root\cimv2") do os over wmi~ExecQuery("select Caption, Version from Win32_OperatingSystem") say os~Caption os~Version end do d over wmi~ExecQuery("select DeviceID, FreeSpace from Win32_LogicalDisk where DriveType = 3") say d~DeviceID (d~FreeSpace % 2**30) "GB free" end
::requires "net.cls"

section.para: How it works. .net~getObject("winmgmts:") is WMI, through a moniker, as .OLEObject~GetObject gives it; its queries are walked with DO OVER. A property without a value is &nil;.
See also Reference, COM Objects (Windows), Objects That Already Exist.
